How About a Widebody New-Gen BMW 3 Series (G50)?
8 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
There is an entirely new 3 Series in BMW’s portfolio, and due to the Neue Klasse design, it is one of the most controversial ever.
Usually, petrolheads either love it or hate it, as there is no in between, and it has been criticized countless times. But the company poured a huge amount of money into its development, so it wasn’t going to retire it early. Thus, production recently commenced at the Dingolfing factory in Germany for the regular model, whereas its long wheelbase variant comes to life in China.
BMW’s new-gen 3 Series has been discussed numerous times, just like other Neue Klasse models, so this story isn’t about reminding you that the exterior design is on the controversial side of things, nor to put the spotlight on the minimalist interior, which is quite quirky to be honest. Instead, this story is about a tuned example. Actually, make that a virtually tuned one, because the car you see in the gallery does not exist.
Not yet, anyway, because we reckon most big tuners out there, as well as a few small ones, are preparing all kinds of upgrades for the G50 as we speak. In this case, the CGI project was signed by @ildar_project and shared on social media a few days ago, featuring the yellow daytime running lights that are available (on the M350 xDrive), and a very aggressive makeover on the outside that makes it look a lot more muscular.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project In addition to the fender flares, this particular ride has skits on the lower parts of the body, new trim on the front fenders, and an entirely new hood. The kidney grille has been virtually altered to the point where it somewhat reminds us of the demised i8. The front and rear bumpers feature plenty of changes, too. A sportier ducktail spoiler sits on the trunk lid, and the diffuser has a pair of extra brake lights integrated into it.
Due to the black finish, this BMW M350 xDrive does not look controversial at all, though let’s not forget that this color tends to hide quirky designs like a champ. The wheels are definitely not bad. They are concave, have a Y-spoke pattern, a silver finish, and are a lot bigger than the OEM ones. A look inside is not a thing, because this digital illustration set is all about the exterior of the car.
Before inviting you to reveal your opinion on this virtually-tuned machine, we will remind you that the new BMW M350 xDrive has 437 hp (352 kW /443 ps) and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm) of torque to play with. The familiar twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six enables 0-60 mph (97 kph) in 4.1 seconds, and that makes it just as fast as the outgoing M3 in its most basic version. So, is this thing a yay or a nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)
